title: Properties of Compounds and Chemical Formulas
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Properties of Compounds and Chemical Formulas Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: The properties of ionic, covalent and metallic substances (melting point, conductivity, solubility) depend on their bonding; chemical formulas show the elements and the ratio of atoms in a compound. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 9, Quarter 4: Science of Materials)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Science of Materials): bonding and properties, writing formulas, naming compounds and counting atoms. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Ionic compounds have high melting points and conduct when molten or dissolved.
key_sub: A formula shows the ratio of atoms.
body_html:
How to think about it

Ionic compounds form giant lattices of ions, so they have high melting points and conduct electricity only when molten or dissolved. Simple covalent substances have low melting points and do not conduct. Metals conduct because of delocalized electrons.

A chemical formula shows which elements are in a compound and how many atoms of each: H₂O has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. The formula of an ionic compound balances the charges: Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ give MgCl₂.

Example

Formula of aluminum oxide?

Al³⁺ and O²⁻

Answer: Al₂O₃

Example

Does solid salt conduct electricity?

Ions cannot move.

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking ionic compounds conduct when solid.
  • Writing charges in the formula.
  • Thinking covalent substances always have low melting points (diamond does not).

faq.a: The dissolved ions can move and carry charge.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of the S<sup>2−</sup> ion?
items.e: The ion has 18 electrons, the same arrangement as a noble gas.

items.q: What is the electronic configuration of the Li<sup>+</sup> ion?
items.e: The ion has 2 electrons, the same arrangement as a noble gas.

items.q: What is the formula of aluminum sulfide?
items.e: Al<sup>3+</sup> and S<sup>2−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is Al<sub>2</sub>S<sub>3</sub>.

items.q: What is the formula of lithium fluoride?
items.e: Li<sup>+</sup> and F<sup>−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is LiF.

items.q: What is the formula of the ion formed by nitrogen?
items.e: Nitrogen (Z = 7) gains 3 electrons.

items.q: What is the formula of potassium chloride?
items.e: K<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is KCl.

items.q: What kind of bond forms between chlorine (Cl) and carbon (C)?
items.e: Two non-metals share electrons.

items.q: What is the formula of potassium nitride?
items.e: K<sup>+</sup> and N<sup>3−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is K<sub>3</sub>N.

items.q: What is the formula of the ion formed by calcium?
items.e: Calcium (Z = 20) loses 2 electrons.

items.q: What is the formula of aluminum chloride?
items.e: Al<sup>3+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is AlCl<sub>3</sub>.

items.q: Al<sup>3+</sup> and O<sup>2−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 2 × (+3) + 3 × (−2) = 0.

items.q: What kind of bond forms between lead (Pb) and tin (Sn)?
items.e: Metal atoms share a sea of electrons.

items.q: What kind of bond forms between tin (Sn) and copper (Cu)?
items.e: Metal atoms share a sea of electrons.

items.q: What kind of bond forms between zinc (Zn) and lead (Pb)?
items.e: Metal atoms share a sea of electrons.

items.q: What is the formula of sodium chloride?
items.e: Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is NaCl.

items.q: What kind of bond forms between copper (Cu) and sulfur (S)?
items.e: A metal gives electrons to a non-metal.

items.q: Ba<sup>2+</sup> and Br<sup>−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 1 × (+2) + 2 × (−1) = 0.

items.q: What kind of bond forms between magnesium (Mg) and phosphorus (P)?
items.e: A metal gives electrons to a non-metal.

items.q: What is the formula of lithium sulfide?
items.e: Lithium forms Li<sup>+</sup> and sulfur forms S<sup>2−</sup>; the charges must add to zero.

items.q: What is the formula of potassium sulfide?
items.e: K<sup>+</sup> and S<sup>2−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is K<sub>2</sub>S.

items.q: What is an alloy?
c: a mixture of a metal with other elements, such as steel (iron and carbon)
items.e: Different-sized atoms stop layers sliding, so alloys are harder.

items.q: A polymer chain is made of 2,000 units of vinyl chloride (C₂H₃Cl, 62.5 g/mol). About what is its molar mass?
A polymer chain is made of 2,000 units of propene (C₃H₆, 42 g/mol). About what is its molar mass?
Crude oil is separated into fractions at a refinery. Which property is used?
items.e: Smaller hydrocarbons boil at lower temperatures.

items.q: Which type of bonding is found in water molecules?
items.e: Non-metals share electron pairs.

items.q: Why do the boiling points of the noble gases increase down the group?
c: there are more electrons, so van der Waals forces are stronger
items.e: Bigger atoms have bigger induced dipole–dipole forces.

items.q: A polymer chain is made of 1,000 units of propene (C₃H₆, 42 g/mol). About what is its molar mass?
A polymer chain is made of 10,000 units of propene (C₃H₆, 42 g/mol). About what is its molar mass?
Why does diamond have a very high melting point?
c: many strong covalent bonds must be broken
items.e: Diamond is a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure.

items.q: What kind of structure does iodine have?
items.e: Weak van der Waals forces between I₂ molecules, so it sublimes easily.

items.q: What is a co-ordinate (dative covalent) bond?
c: a bond with three shared pairs
a shared pair of electrons where both electrons come from one atom
items.e: For example the bond from N to H⁺ in NH₄⁺.

items.q: Why does magnesium have a higher melting point than sodium?
c: Mg²⁺ has a larger charge and there are more delocalized electrons
items.e: Stronger metallic bonding.

items.q: Many styrene monomers are linked in a long chain. Which polymer forms?
items.e: Polymers are chains of repeating monomers.

items.q: Many ethene monomers are linked in a long chain. Which polymer forms?
items.e: Polymers are chains of repeating monomers.

items.q: Why are metals malleable?
c: the ions repel each other strongly
layers of cations can slide over each other while the delocalized electrons keep holding them together
items.e: Metallic bonding is not directional.

items.q: A polymer chain is made of 1,000 units of styrene (C₈H₈, 104 g/mol). About what is its molar mass?
Which molecule is polar?
items.e: CO₂, CCl₄ and BF₃ are symmetrical, so the dipoles cancel.

items.q: What is the strongest type of intermolecular force?
items.e: Covalent bonds are within molecules, not between them.

items.q: How many lone pairs of electrons are on the central atom in SF<sub>4</sub>?
items.e: SF4: 4 bonding pairs and 1 lone pairs.

items.q: What is a nanomaterial?
c: a material more than 1 mm thick
a material with particles or structures 1–100 nm in size
items.e: Nanoparticles have a very large surface area to volume ratio.

items.q: What is the octet rule?
c: Atoms tend to gain, lose or share electrons to have 8 in their outer shell.
items.e: Hydrogen and helium need 2.

items.q: What happens in a covalent bond?
c: Two atoms share a pair of electrons.
One atom gives away all its electrons.
items.e: Non-metal + non-metal.

items.q: What is the formula of strontium fluoride?
items.e: Strontium forms Sr<sup>2+</sup> and fluorine forms F<sup>−</sup>; the charges must add to zero.

items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: What holds a metal together?

items.e: Metallic bonding.

items.q: What is a molecule?
c: a group of atoms held together by covalent bonds

items.q: Why do nanoparticles often behave differently from the bulk material?
c: they have a much larger surface area to volume ratio
they are made of different elements
items.e: Zinc oxide nanoparticles in sunscreen look clear, not white.

items.q: How can pure water be obtained from sea water?
items.e: Water evaporates and condenses; salt is left behind.

items.q: Why is an alloy usually harder than the pure metal?
c: atoms of different sizes disrupt the layers so they cannot slide easily
items.e: Bronze and steel are harder than copper and iron.

items.q: How can sand be separated from salt water?
items.e: Insoluble solids stay on the filter paper.

items.q: Why do atoms form bonds?
c: to reach a more stable, full outer shell
items.e: Usually 8 valence electrons (octet).

items.q: Mark studies making ammonia: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3. How many nitrogen atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: Diane studies rusting of iron: 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3. How many iron atoms are in the products (right side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 4.

items.q: Hazel studies rusting of iron: 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3. How many oxygen atoms are in the products (right side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 6.

items.q: Dennis writes 4C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>. How many carbon atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 4 multiplies everything: 4 × 3 = 12.

items.q: Mae studies photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2. How many carbon atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 6.

items.q: Patricia looks up nitrogen gas, N<sub>2</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 2 nitrogen = 2 atoms.

items.q: Diane looks up carbon dioxide, CO<sub>2</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 1 carbon + 2 oxygen = 3 atoms.

items.q: Angel looks up oxygen gas, O<sub>2</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 2 oxygen = 2 atoms.

items.q: Christian writes 3CH<sub>4</sub>. How many carbon atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 3 multiplies everything: 3 × 1 = 3.

items.q: Kristine studies rusting of iron: 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3. How many oxygen atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 6.

items.q: Angelo studies magnesium burning: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. How many oxygen atoms are in the products (right side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: Kevin studies hydrogen burning: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O. How many oxygen atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: Jomar writes 4H<sub>2</sub>O. How many oxygen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 4 multiplies everything: 4 × 1 = 4.

items.q: Diane writes 4C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O. How many oxygen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 4 multiplies everything: 4 × 1 = 4.

items.q: Kyla looks up ethanol, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 2 carbon + 6 hydrogen + 1 oxygen = 9 atoms.

items.q: How many carbon atoms are in one molecule of glucose (sugar), C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>?
items.e: The subscript after C is 6.

items.q: Rose looks up hydrogen peroxide, H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 2 hydrogen + 2 oxygen = 4 atoms.

items.q: Ca<sup>2+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 1 × (+2) + 2 × (−1) = 0.

items.q: Isabel looks up calcium carbonate (chalk), CaCO<sub>3</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 1 calcium + 1 carbon + 3 oxygen = 5 atoms.

items.q: What is the formula of sodium sulfide?
items.e: Sodium forms Na<sup>+</sup> and sulfur forms S<sup>2−</sup>; the charges must add to zero.
